question.text: Roshni Trust's SIA report describes its intervention as 'empowering 12,000 children with disabilities'. The SIA wants to test whether the claim qualifies as 'direct impact' per Chapter 7.3.2. Which test is MOST relevant?

answer.text: Whether the change is observed in the intended target group in the immediate time frame and flows from a taxonomic SAS classification
Whether the SE has published the number on its website
Whether the number exceeds the 67% FPE threshold
Whether the number is a multiple of the 16 eligible activities under SEBI ICDR 292B

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7.3.2 defines direct impact as 'changes seen as a result of the intervention in the intended target group who are also the key stakeholders' and adds that 'Each taxonomic classification (within the SASs) will guide the set of indicators'. Direct impacts appear in the immediate time frame. The Trap: A is a visibility test, not an impact test. C and D invent regulatory thresholds that do not apply to impact-classification. Cross-Exam Context: Target-group and materiality concepts cross with SAS-500 (environment) and SAS-1300 (financial inclusion) in Topic 6. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reviewing direct-impact claims, require a SAS-tag per indicator in the impact scorecard. If a claimed direct impact cannot be mapped back to a SAS taxonomy line, it probably belongs in a narrative footnote, not the direct-impact table.
